name: PagerDuty, Inc.

profile.description: PagerDuty, founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, operates a digital operations management platform spanning incident management, AIOps event correlation, automation (Rundeck-based), customer service operations and generative/agentic AI, with 750+ integrations. Q2 FY2027 (July 2026) revenue was $124.4M (+0.8% YoY) with ARR of $501M, 15,506 paid customers and 884 customers above $100K ARR. John DiLullo became CEO on May 11, 2026, with founder-era CEO Jennifer Tejada moving to Executive Chair.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): PagerDuty has expanded from on-call alerting into an Operations Cloud — AIOps, Rundeck-based automation, customer service ops and generative AI — and now positions itself as an 'AI-first' platform that orchestrates AI agents across 750+ integrations [1][4]; the new lines broadened the platform but have not reaccelerated growth. AI Deployment (2/2): AI products are shipping — Q2 FY2027 brought upgrades to the autonomous SRE agent, incident lifecycle integration and an agentic on-call shift management offering, with early customer adoption reported [1][2]. Market Share (1/2): A recognized incident-management leader with 884 $100K+ customers, but dollar-based net retention of 98% and 0.8% revenue growth indicate stable-to-slipping share [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Named agent products are rolling out, but no launch dates or revenue targets tied to them are disclosed and FY2027 revenue is guided flat at $491.5-496.5M [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D was $126.9M in FY2026, 25.8% of $492.5M revenue, top-quartile for application software [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): PagerDuty's purpose centers on helping teams keep critical digital services running and 'revolutionize how critical work gets done' — clear about what it does but not distinctive [2]. Community Impact (1/2): The company runs its PagerDuty.org social-impact program and publishes impact reports with an ESG steering committee and an EcoVadis silver rating, but no dollar-quantified giving was found in this screen [3]. Employee Retention (0/2): No tenure or turnover data found; the company referenced a recent restructuring and replaced its CEO and CFO in 2026 [1][2]. Insider Buying (0/2): No open-market insider purchases since the 2019 IPO; Executive Chair Jennifer Tejada sold roughly 1.03M shares between May and October 2026 (e.g., 358,400 at $6.98 and 302,100 at $10.70) [6].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanical score (Growth sleeve; forward PEG unavailable from yfinance and excluded, leaving 8 weight units). Liquidity floor passed: 1.56M avg shares x $16.71 = ~$26M/day [4]. D/E 167.2% -> 0.58; ROE 82.6% -> 1.00 (x2); revenue growth YoY 0.8% -> 0.69; 5yr revenue CAGR 18.2% (FY2021 $213.6M to FY2026 $492.5M, derived from FMP) -> 1.00 (x2); forward P/E 11.4 -> 1.00; profit margin 37.5% -> 1.00 [4][5]. Weighted sum 7.27 / 8 = 9.1 -> 9. Caveat: trailing ROE and margin are inflated by a $152.5M FY2026 income tax benefit (valuation-allowance release) on just $5.8M of GAAP operating income; Q2 FY2027 GAAP net income was $4.7M while free cash flow was a healthier $32.8M [1][5].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9 — EXPOSED): PagerDuty sells per-seat incident-response software, a workflow that AI SRE agents (its own and competitors') are designed to automate; revenue growth has stalled at 0.8% with 98% net retention, and the stock fell below $7 in May 2026 before recovering, reflecting market concern that agentic AI and observability-platform bundling compress standalone incident tools [1][6]. Its defenses are 750+ integrations, enterprise switching costs and system-of-record status for incident data, and CEO DiLullo argues PagerDuty is 'uniquely positioned to benefit' as AI changes how software is operated [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI agent products are shipping, but no AI-specific revenue or usage metrics are disclosed [1].

infinite_game.summary: PagerDuty serves a worthwhile purpose — keeping the digital services people depend on running — but in Sinek's terms it is playing a finite game today: a 2026 CEO and CFO turnover, a restructuring, flat revenue, repeated sale explorations (2023-2025) and heavy insider selling describe a company optimizing for margin and exit value rather than a cause. The AI-first agent pivot shows adaptability, but it reads as a defensive response to disruption.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The mission to revolutionize how critical work gets done is service-oriented but generic, and current communication emphasizes ARR crossing $500M, non-GAAP margins of 25-26% and EPS guidance rather than a future state worth sacrificing for [1][2]. The company explored a sale in late 2023, January 2024 and July 2025, which Sinek would read as a finite orientation [7].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management has re-architected the product around AI agents (autonomous SRE agent, agentic on-call management) and kept R&D at ~26% of revenue through a growth stall [1][5]. However, the restructuring and margin-expansion focus (non-GAAP operating margin guided up to 25-26%) suggest near-term earnings are being prioritized alongside the bet [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): 2026 brought a CEO change (Tejada to Executive Chair, outsider John DiLullo as CEO), a new CFO, the CFO's retirement and a restructuring, while the Executive Chair has sold over 1M shares [1][2][6]. Glassdoor shows a middling 3.6/5 with 63% recommending, consistent with an unsettled environment rather than a high-trust one [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): PagerDuty has evolved from alerting to an operations platform with automation and AIOps and is now repositioning as an AI-agent orchestration layer [1][4]. These are meaningful adjacent extensions, but the company has not abandoned its core seat-based incident business, and the pivot has yet to restore growth.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found framing competitors as teachers; messaging focuses on PagerDuty being 'uniquely positioned' and on integrations breadth, while the company has repeatedly sought acquirers [1][7].

investment_thesis: The bull case is a cheap, cash-generative platform in transition: PagerDuty trades at 11.4x forward earnings with $470.0M of cash and investments, posted its fifth straight GAAP-profitable quarter, generated $32.8M of Q2 free cash flow, crossed $501M ARR, and raised its FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin guide to 25-26% with EPS of $1.33-1.37 [1][4]. Its autonomous SRE agent and agentic on-call products give it a credible role orchestrating AI agents in incident response, and recurring buyer interest (sale explorations in 2023-2025) suggests strategic value that could cap downside [1][7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that AI and platform bundling are eroding the core: revenue grew just 0.8% to $124.4M, dollar-based net retention is 98%, FY2027 revenue is guided roughly flat at $491.5-496.5M, and no AI revenue is disclosed [1]. Reported profitability is flattered by a $152.5M FY2026 tax benefit, D/E is 167%, leadership turned over in 2026, and the Executive Chair has sold more than 1M shares this year — signals that insiders are not underwriting a reacceleration [5][6].
key_catalysts: Monetization of agentic AI — autonomous SRE agent and agentic on-call management launched in Q2 FY2027; any disclosed AI ARR would reframe the growth story [1]
Margin expansion — Q3 FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin guided to 26.5-27.5% and EPS of $0.34-0.36 versus Q2's 23.7% and $0.32 [1]
Strategic interest — PagerDuty hired Qatalyst after receiving inbound sponsor and strategic interest in 2025; renewed M&A activity could re-rate the shares [7]
key_risks: AI substitution and bundling — AI SRE agents from observability and ITSM platforms could compress demand for standalone, seat-priced incident tools, as 98% net retention already suggests [1]
Leadership transition — new CEO (May 2026) and CFO plus a restructuring raise execution risk during a product pivot [1][2]
Earnings quality — FY2026 net income of $173.9M was driven by a $152.5M tax benefit; GAAP operating margin was only 8.2% in Q2 FY2027 [1][5]
